title: PH, Chile sign free trade deal amid APEC 2026 summit
summary: The Philippines and Chile on Thursday formally signed their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) on the sidelines of the 33rd AELM, or the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC)…

blocks.text: SHENZHEN, China — The Philippines and Chile on Thursday formally signed their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) on the sidelines of the 33rd AELM, or the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
The signing was led by Philippine President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast during a bilateral meeting held at the Shenzhen International Exchange Center.
Marcos said the signing of the free trade deal was something that the Philippines "very much hoped for."
"We're very happy that we have finally come to a formal agreement," the Philippine President said.

"The FTA is going to provide us with a very, very important foundation to build on to make this trade, this relationship, not only in trade, not only between governments, but between our people—stronger, more vibrant, and deeper," he added.
CEPA, the Philippines' first free trade agreement (FTA) with a Latin American nation, seeks to promote the exchange of goods, services, and investments between Manila and Santiago.

According to the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), the key benefits of the CEPA include the reduction of tariff and non-tariff barriers to promote trade between the two countries, and the opening of better market access for Philippine products in Chile and vice versa.
Marcos also underscored that the FTA with Chile has taken "a very important priority" in the economic planning of the Philippines.

"I think that it is now time that Philippines and Chile look to the future and find ways to engage, and as we are we were studying the situation more and more, we see that there's many there are many things that can be done between Chile and the Philippines," he added. — VDV, GMA News
